newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania protests Italy resignation call.
newsitem.headline: Albania protests Italy resignation call.

text.p: Albania issued a strong diplomatic protest on Tuesday to Italy after Rome's deputy foreign minister said the Italian government believed Albanian President Sali Berisha should leave office but would not push for his departure now.

In a statement released on the state-controlled news agency ATA, the Albanian Foreign Ministry said: "We energetically protest against this unacceptable interference in the internal affairs from the Italian Foreign Ministry through the statements of deputy foreign minister (Piero) Fassino...who is asking for the dismissal of the Albanian President."

The protest note was handed by the Foreign Ministry to the Italian embassy in Tirana. While praising Italy for its relief contributions to the strife-ridden country, Albania called the Itanian comments unacceptable outside interference.

"This sort of interference in Albania's internal affairs is all the more unacceptable at a time when it is Italy itself that will have command of the multinational force that will come to Albania," the statement said.
"Albania is a sovereign state and it is its sovereign right to decide on the legimate sovereign institutions of the country according to the constitutional laws of the Albanian state."

In Rome earlier, deputy foreign minister Fassino told a leadership meeting of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), the biggest party in the coalition: "That Berisha should go is very clear, at least to us. And when I say us I'm not just talking about the PDS. I'm also talking about the government."
